persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Özkent devotes most of today's video to the Financial Times' OpenAI report: when the FT wrote that annualized revenue was $50 billion rather than $70 billion, **Nasdaq** fell 1.25%, **Oracle** 5.5%, **Broadcom** 4.4%, **Nvidia** 3% and **SMH** 3.4%. In his view it is an accounting-standard difference: gross revenue is $70 billion, net is $50 billion after commissions, and nothing has changed. He sees the drop as a buying opportunity, says he bought some **Oracle**, and criticizes Goldman's buy rating on **Palantir** at $200 with a $230 target.

On macro, he says Treasury auction demand came in above expectations, that yields have peaked and he expects them to fall from here, which is positive for **Bitcoin** and **gold**. He reads Trump saying he won't attack Iran until the midterms as good news for markets, and **oil** is retreating. He expects **SpaceX** to rise at the open despite the spectrum news; he also describes an AI-assisted panel he built to track the midterms.

items.title: Ekonomi Basını Yatırımcıları Nasıl Kandırıyor?
items.summary: Özkent calls the Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is $50 billion rather than $70 billion a misreading of accounting standards. The $70 billion reported in August was gross (commissions included) to compare with Anthropic, while $50 billion is the net figure; the $20 billion difference is commissions paid to distributors like AWS and Azure. Nasdaq fell as much as 1.75% intraday, Oracle 5.5%, Broadcom 4.4%, Nvidia 3% and SMH 3.4%; Özkent says he sees the drop as a buying opportunity and bought some Oracle. He explains Goldman's buy rating on Palantir at $200 with a $230 target by analysts' fear of being wrong. He says oil fell after Trump said he won't attack Iran until the midterms and thinks the war is practically over if Trump loses the House/Senate; he has built an election panel starting from a 53-47 Senate. Demand at the 30-year Treasury auction was about 2.5 times the expected level and also high at the 10-year; he sees yields peaking and expects a decline, which is positive for Bitcoin and gold. He notes carrier stocks fell sharply after SpaceX bought US spectrum and expects SpaceX to rise at the open. Michigan confidence, jobless claims and Fed meeting news are the items to watch; he thinks the market has bottomed.

persons.name: Berk Dinçtürk
persons.digest:
Dinçtürk says the soft inflation print was manipulated through its composition and that the gap between official and real inflation is widening, similar to the Arthur Burns era. After unemployment rose to 4.2%, the chance of an October rate hike was taken off the table; in his view Trump replacing the head of the statistics agency played a role.

The **US Dollar Index** fell from 110 to 102, and he does not believe a US with $40 trillion in debt will make the dollar appreciate permanently; he says the decline will continue until the end of Trump's term.

items.title: ''Trump Dönemi Sonuna Kadar Dolar Endeksi Değer Kaybetmeye Devam Edecektir'' | Berk Dinçtürk
items.summary: Dinçtürk says the inflation print came in soft because its composition was manipulated and that the gap between official and real inflation is widening like in the Arthur Burns era. He relays that after unemployment rose to 4.2% the chance of an October rate hike was removed, that Trump fired the statistics agency head last year, installed his own man and insists rates must fall. He notes headlines saying the president wants to weaken the dollar on one side and that the Fed will hike three or four times on the other; he does not believe a US with $40 trillion in debt will make the dollar appreciate permanently. The dollar index was at 110 when Trump took office and is at 102 today, a drop of about 10%. He says the dollar index will keep losing value until the end of Trump's term.

assets.note: Says the dollar index, down from 110 to 102, will keep losing value until the end of Trump's term.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent, Broadcom's 4.4% drop stemmed from a misreading of the accounting in the OpenAI revenue report; he gave no new buy/sell level.
holdings.opinion: OpenAI-linked demand is the core thesis for Broadcom; if the news is clarified the sharp drop makes little sense, otherwise AI chip orders get questioned. What matters is how the OpenAI revenue debate resolves.
ai_points: For: per Özkent the $70B vs. $50B gap that triggered the drop is an accounting-standard difference.
Against: the roughly 14% weight and dependence on OpenAI let one headline move the stock about 4%.
Against: with narrow leadership, AI chip stocks are exposed to pullbacks.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: I think we have reached the peak in yields. I expect a decline from here.

holdings.why: Bora Özkent says he sees a peak in yields while WallStDiaries flags a 5.5% risk on the 10-year; there is no firm level/date.
holdings.opinion: The long-duration bond fund carries the bet on peak yields; it benefits if Özkent is right, but price losses grow in a 5.5% scenario. Watch whether Treasury auction demand continues.

Against: per WallStDiaries the 10-year yield is at 5.29% with a 5.5% risk.
Against: long duration is very sensitive to rising rates.
